title: Coverage Months a Billing Cycle Carries on a Rider Premium Charge
content:
How many coverage months one rider premium charge carries under the Optional Supplemental Benefit Riders follows from the member's Medicare Advantage Health Plans enrollment — whether it stands in force and how often it is billed.

## The rule

**Where the medical plan enrollment the rider hangs on stands in force and is billed quarterly**, one charge carries three coverage months.

**Where that enrollment does not stand in force and a rider premium charge already stands on the rider premium account**, one charge carries the whole calendar months from the day the rider took effect to the handling date, and never fewer than one.

**Otherwise**, one charge carries the single coverage month it is booked to.

## Condition and coverage months

| What the Medicare Advantage Health Plans enrollment shows | What the rider premium account shows | Coverage months one charge carries |
|---|---|---|
| In force, billed quarterly | Anything | 3 |
| In force, billed other than quarterly | Anything | 1 |
| Not in force | At least one rider premium charge already standing | The whole calendar months from the day the rider took effect to the handling date, never fewer than 1 |
| Not in force | No rider premium charge standing | 1 |

## Worked on hypothetical inputs

- An enrollment standing in force and billed quarterly: 3 coverage months.
- An enrollment no longer standing in force, one charge already on the rider premium account, the rider having taken effect 7 whole calendar months before the handling date: 7 coverage months.
- An enrollment no longer standing in force, one charge already standing, the rider having taken effect in the month of handling: 1 coverage month, that being the floor.
- An enrollment standing in force and billed monthly: 1 coverage month.
